newsitem.title: UK: Sterling strength to prove temporary, BOE says.
newsitem.headline: Sterling strength to prove temporary, BOE says.

text.p: Sterling's recent strength is likely to prove temporary and has no implications for British inflation in the medium term, the Bank of England said in its quarterly inflation report on Wednesday.
But it said the strong pound increased significantly the short run uncertainty about RPIX inflation.

"The monetary factors underlying sterling's strength -- a perceived tightening of UK monetary conditions and a perceived loosening of overseas monetary conditions -- are probably temporary," the report said.

The Bank's chief economist, Mervyn King, said: "We should not set an easier monetary policy now because of sterling's strength. We do not believe in any rule of thumb relating a change in exchange rates to a change in interest rates."

The Bank noted that about two percent of the pound's recent rise occurred on October 30, when a surprise quarter percentage point rise in British interest rates was made, and on the two following days.
The report said that the pound's rise, about nine percent on a trade weighted basis since early August, did not have implications for inflation in the medium term.

"The loosening in overseas monetary conditions would lead to a rise in foreign prices which, in the long run, would exactly match the fall in UK prices brought about by the higher exchange rate," the Bank said.
But the Bank did note short-term risks.
"Both the observed rise in inflation and the appreciation of sterling increased significantly the short-run uncertainty about RPIX inflation," the report said.
King said underlying inflation could push above three percent in the next month or so.
"There must be a concern that if this exchange rate persists there will be a growing imbalance between domestic and export demand," King said.
